newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libyan congress cracks down on rebel sympathisers.
newsitem.headline: Libyan congress cracks down on rebel sympathisers.

text.p: Libya's General People's Congress has decided to punish villages or tribes which refuse to denounce "terrorists", state television reported.
On Sunday Libyan television, monitored in Tunis, broadcast live debates in the congress which agreed by acclamation to impose collective punishments such as cutting off water or electricity supplies.
It was not clear why the congress took this step, as there have been no official reports of any troubles in the country.
But exiled Libyan fundamentalists leaders reported last year that Moslem rebel groups had carried out several attacks against government forces. The reports were not confirmed independently.
During the congress's session, which took place in the coastal city of Sirte, hardliners and liberals debated who would hand down the punishments to villages.

Prime Minister Abdelmajid al-Gu'ud, supported by Saad Mujber, head of the foreign affairs department at the Congress, insisted any decisions be taken by courts and not by popular committees as stated in the congressional motion.
"When it is proven that a group has committed something, it is up to the People's Court to issue a sentence for execution," Gu'ud said.
"We are a state of law and we must act within the law. Whatever decision is taken must be taken by a court," Mujber said.

But Ahmed Mohamed Ibrahim, coordinator for the about 400 grassroots People's Congresses and the man who read the motion to the assembly, said that what he called the "people's power", established by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, was superior to the law.
"The popular will is stronger than the law. The masses are able to decide. The court is not necessarily the single means to exert the people's power," he said.

Under Libyan law, courts are the only places for trials of criminals. But followers of Gaddafi in popular committees have been challenging this, claiming the right to punish anti-revolutionary political "criminals".
